summary: The main article describes a visible light-mediated oxidative decarboxylation of aminoarylacetic acids to generate benzyl radicals for addition to electron-deficient alkenes. It includes three tables detailing optimization of reaction conditions and substrate scope, and three schemes illustrating the reaction mechanism and comparative studies.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Oxidative decarboxylation of carboxylic acids bearing an amino group.
items.description: Compares the known decarboxylation of alpha-amino acids with the proposed decarboxylation of aminoarylacetic acids to form benzyl radicals.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Photochemical reactions of 4-(N,N-dimethylamino)phenylacetic acid (1a) with ethyl (E)-2-cyano-3-phenylpropenoate (2a)
items.description: Optimization table showing the effects of different photocatalysts and solvents on the yield of the benzylated product 3a.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Photochemical reactions of arylacetic acids (1) with 2a
items.description: Explores the scope of various arylacetic acids bearing different amino groups at the para-position in the reaction with alkene 2a.

items.heading: Table 3
items.caption: Photochemical reactions of arylacetic acids (1d or 1g) with alkenes (2)
items.description: Demonstrates the substrate scope of various electron-deficient alkenes reacting with specific aminoarylacetic acids.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Effect of the position of the amino group on reactions of 1d, 1d', and 1d'' with 2a.
items.description: Shows that only the para-substituted aminoarylacetic acid undergoes successful decarboxylative addition, while meta and ortho isomers do not.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Plausible reaction pathway.
items.description: Illustrates the proposed catalytic cycle involving single electron oxidation, decarboxylation, radical addition, and reduction.
